messages:
nina: SIEM alert just flagged an abnormal bulk read pattern against customer_db replicas starting ~11:02 UTC, high bytes out for ~13m. Possible mass export.
sec-bot: ALERT: db.bytes_out anomaly detected for service_account=analytics-exporter, threshold exceeded (x18). Link: https://siem.internal/alerts/7721 :rotating_light:
sam: Can you paste the top query samples from the audit log?
nina: grabbing now — looks like repeated paginated selects against customers.orders and customers.profiles. Not slow queries, lots of rows each. snippet: ```SELECT * FROM customers.profiles WHERE id > 0 ORDER BY id LIMIT 10000 OFFSET 0;``` repeated with increasing OFFSET.
priya: Who owns analytics-exporter service account? I think it's used by data-warehouse ETL but shouldn't run ad-hoc against production replicas.
lucas: It maps to svc-analytics in k8s in prod-us-east. Last deployed ~2w ago by jamal.
maria: tagging compliance — need to know if any PII columns were selected. Please preserve audit logs.
sam: Query plan shows full table scans on profiles (no predicate), returned ~2.4M rows over 13m window. We should assume PII touched until proven otherwise.
nina: Containment: I'm going to rotate creds for svc-analytics and revoke the service account token. Priya, can you block egress from that k8s service to DB host for now?
priya: On it. Applying network policy to deny cluster role svc-analytics -> db-prod replicas. Expected completion in 30s. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sec-bot: ACTION: rotated service account token for svc-analytics (nina). Network policy applied (priya).
lucas: Also paused scheduled ETL job on data-warehouse for svc-analytics to avoid retries.
sam: Snapshotting DB replica audit logs and creating export of query fingerprints. Storing to secure bucket with KMS key redwood-incident-2024 for review.
maria: Please run a quick mapping of returned columns to our sensitive-data catalog (PII/PCI). I need a preliminary impact statement for legal.
nina: Will do. Early look: profiles.email, profiles.full_name, orders.billing_address appeared in a subset of rows.
priya: Verified no other services are exhibiting similar traffic. This appears scoped to svc-analytics credentials.
lucas: Any signs of credential compromise vs misconfiguration? Who has access to service account keys?
nina: Jamal had created the token; CI job stash also had a copy in a repo that should have been secret-scanned. Investigating if that repo had a leaked token.
sam: Searching commit history now. If token in git, rotate KMS key and rotate DB user password too.
maria: Also include timeline: earliest access observed 10:58 UTC, last 11:15 UTC. Need to notify Data Protection Officer if confirmed PII exfil.
priya: Quick mitigation checklist: 1) revoke token (done) 2) block network (done) 3) pause ETL (done) 4) rotate DB creds -> I'll schedule with infra 5) rotate KMS wrapping key for incident artifacts (sam + nina)
nina: Next steps for triage: - sam: produce list of affected customer IDs and columns -> secure bucket - priy a: confirm no other tokens reused - lucas: contact jamal for how token was created - maria: draft initial comms for legal and CDP
sam: Uploaded audit snapshot to gs://redwood-sec-incidents/1729501234/audit-snapshot.log (encrypted). Tagged with redwood-incident-2024 KMS.
nina: Checking the bucket now, pulling sample rows to determine sensitivity. Will not paste data in Slack.
maria: Legal asked for an estimate of affected customers. Please provide counts and whether SSNs or payment tokens are included.
priya: I ran a quick grep on the snapshot: no columns named ssn or card_number returned, but billing_address and email showed up. Still sensitive.
lucas: Jamal says token was generated manually during a one-off backfill and never rotated. We're updating runbook to forbid long-lived tokens in repos and require short-lived KMS-wrapped secrets.
sam: Post-incident actions I recommend: enforce RBAC so svc accounts have least privilege, enable row-level filtering for analytics service, add SIEM rule for pagination-pattern exports, and increase audit_log retention.
maria: Good. For comms, we'll run an internal incident summary first then decide customer notification scope. Legal will advise.
priya: I'll open a follow-up Jira for infra tasks (rotate DB creds, rotate KMS key, rotate any leaked repo secrets) and tag everyone.
nina: Final note: no signs of external exfil (no outbound to external IPs). Evidence points to internal misuse or accidental long-lived credential used for large backfill. Closing containment; keeping incident open for root cause and remediation. :white_check_mark:
sec-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: status=contained, owner=nina, incident_id=IR-2024-087
nina: Thanks all — great fast response. We'll reconvene in 24h with root cause writeup and runbook changes.
